description: The mathematics and engineering of secrecy and authenticity: classical ciphers and how they break, block and stream ciphers, public-key cryptography, hashes, MACs, signatures, certificates, key management and the protocols such as TLS that secure the Internet. Taught to the depth of a leading applied cryptography course.
modelledOn: Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice
Katz and Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography
Boneh and Shoup, A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography (selected chapters)
Ferguson, Schneier and Kohno, Cryptography Engineering
outcomes: Break classical ciphers with frequency analysis and explain why modern ciphers resist such attacks.
Describe AES and modes of operation, choose a mode correctly, and implement authenticated encryption.
Explain and implement RSA, Diffie-Hellman and elliptic-curve operations and the number theory behind them.
Use hash functions, MACs and digital signatures for integrity and authentication and explain their security properties.
Describe PKI, certificates and the TLS handshake and analyse the security of a protocol.
Design key management, including generation, distribution, storage and rotation, and recognise common implementation failures.

units.title: Security goals and classical ciphers
topics: Confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, non-repudiation; threat models and Kerckhoffs's principle
Caesar, substitution, Vigenere, Playfair, Hill, transposition ciphers; the Enigma
Cryptanalysis: frequency analysis, Kasiski examination, known- and chosen-plaintext attacks
The one-time pad and perfect secrecy; why keys must be random and unreused
Computational security, security parameters and negligible probabilities

units.title: Number theory for cryptography
topics: Modular arithmetic, groups, Euler's totient, Fermat and Euler theorems
Extended Euclid and modular inverses; fast modular exponentiation
Primality testing (Miller-Rabin), prime generation, the Chinese remainder theorem
Discrete logarithms and the hardness assumptions (factoring, DLP, ECDLP)
Finite fields GF(2^8) as used in AES

units.title: Symmetric encryption: block ciphers, AES and modes
topics: Block cipher design: confusion and diffusion, Feistel networks, DES and its weaknesses, 3DES
AES: SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey, key schedule; implementing a round
Modes of operation: ECB (and the penguin), CBC, CTR, CFB, OFB; padding and padding-oracle attacks
Authenticated encryption: GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305; nonce misuse
Stream ciphers: RC4 history, ChaCha20; pseudo-random generators and CSPRNGs
Side channels: timing, power, cache; constant-time implementation

units.title: Public-key cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman, elliptic curves
topics: The public-key idea; RSA key generation, encryption, decryption and correctness proof
Attacks on textbook RSA; padding (OAEP); key sizes and factoring records
Diffie-Hellman key exchange, man-in-the-middle, authenticated key exchange; ElGamal
Elliptic curves over finite fields, point addition, scalar multiplication, ECDH, Curve25519
Hybrid encryption and key encapsulation; post-quantum cryptography overview (lattices, Kyber)

units.title: Hash functions and MACs
topics: Properties: preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance; the birthday bound
MD5 and SHA-1 breaks; SHA-2, SHA-3; Merkle-Damgard and sponge constructions
Message authentication codes: HMAC, CMAC; MAC-then-encrypt versus encrypt-then-MAC
Password hashing: salts, bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2; rainbow tables
Applications: integrity checking, commitments, blockchains, deduplication

units.title: Digital signatures and PKI
topics: RSA signatures (PSS), DSA, ECDSA, EdDSA; hash-then-sign; nonce reuse disasters
Certificates, X.509, certificate authorities, chains, revocation (CRL, OCSP), Certificate Transparency
Web of trust versus hierarchical PKI; code signing; Ghana's national PKI and e-signature law
Certificate pinning and the risks of mis-issued certificates

units.title: TLS and secure protocols
topics: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 handshakes, cipher suites, forward secrecy, session resumption, 0-RTT
Attacks on TLS history: BEAST, POODLE, Heartbleed, downgrade attacks; configuring a server correctly
SSH, IPsec and VPNs (IKE, WireGuard), Kerberos, S/MIME and PGP, Signal protocol and double ratchet
DNSSEC and DNS over HTTPS; email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
Analysing a protocol: attacker models, replay, reflection, the Needham-Schroeder lesson

units.title: Key management
topics: Key generation and randomness; entropy sources and failures (Debian OpenSSL, low-entropy devices)
Key distribution: KDCs, public-key distribution, key agreement; key hierarchies and derivation (HKDF)
Storage: hardware security modules, TPMs, secure enclaves, key management services; secrets in applications
Rotation, revocation, escrow, backup; secret sharing (Shamir)
Cryptographic policy: algorithms and key lengths, NIST and ECRYPT recommendations

units.title: Applied cryptography and capstone
topics: Using cryptographic libraries correctly: libsodium, OpenSSL, Web Crypto; what not to build yourself
Cryptography in mobile money, banking (EMV, HSMs), messaging and blockchains
Common implementation mistakes and how to review code for them
Capstone: a secure messaging or file-sharing tool with authenticated key exchange and authenticated encryption

schedule.title: Security goals and classical ciphers
schedule.exercise: Write a threat model for a village mobile money agent in half a page, then break a short Caesar and a short substitution cipher by hand.

tasks.title: Encrypt and decrypt a 30-letter message with a Caesar cipher using the maths lab, and brute-force a given ciphertext by trying all 25 shifts
Break a 300-letter monoalphabetic substitution ciphertext using letter frequency analysis and report the key you recover and the steps
Find the key length of a Vigenere ciphertext with a Kasiski examination and index of coincidence, then recover the key and plaintext

schedule.title: One-time pad and computational security
schedule.exercise: Short essay: why a reused one-time pad fails, and why practical ciphers rely on computational rather than perfect security.

tasks.title: Encrypt a short message with a one-time pad using XOR and decrypt it again, checking that a wrong key gives a different plausible message
Recover two plaintexts from two ciphertexts encrypted with the same pad by XORing them together and using crib dragging
Estimate how many years brute force needs for 56, 80 and 128-bit keys at one trillion guesses a second and tabulate what counts as secure

schedule.title: Number theory toolkit
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute modular inverses, fast exponentiation, a CRT reconstruction and a Miller-Rabin test by hand and with code.

tasks.title: Compute the modular inverse of 17 mod 3120 with the extended Euclidean algorithm and verify that the product equals 1 mod 3120
Implement Miller-Rabin and use it to find a 64-bit probable prime, then compare the number of witnesses needed with a Carmichael number
Implement multiplication in GF(2^8) with the AES polynomial and verify that the inverse table matches known values for ten bytes

schedule.title: Block ciphers and AES
schedule.exercise: Trace one full AES round on a given 16-byte state and write a short note on why DES keys are too short.

tasks.title: Run two rounds of a toy Feistel cipher by hand and measure the avalanche effect after flipping one input bit
Implement SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns and AddRoundKey and check one round against a published test vector
Encrypt a bitmap image in ECB and in CBC mode, and mount a padding oracle attack that recovers a plaintext block from error responses

schedule.title: Authenticated encryption and side channels
schedule.exercise: Short analysis: explain why nonce reuse breaks GCM and how a timing side channel leaks a password check.

tasks.title: Encrypt and authenticate a message with a toy authenticated scheme, then flip one ciphertext bit and show the tag check rejects it
Implement a ChaCha20 quarter round and a keystream generator, and show that identical key and nonce yield identical keystreams
Exploit a variable-time string comparison to recover a four-character secret by timing, then rewrite it as a constant-time comparison and retest

schedule.title: RSA and Diffie-Hellman
schedule.exercise: Hand-calculate a small RSA key pair, encrypt and decrypt a number, and draw a man-in-the-middle attack on unauthenticated Diffie-Hellman.

tasks.title: Generate an RSA key pair from p=61 and q=53, encrypt the number 65 and decrypt it again, showing every intermediate value
Break textbook RSA with a small public exponent by taking the cube root, then explain how padding prevents the attack
Simulate Alice and Bob exchanging Diffie-Hellman values through a network where Mallory sits in the middle, and show both derived keys differ

schedule.title: Elliptic curves and post-quantum ideas
schedule.exercise: Short lab: add points on a small curve by hand, and write a half-page note on why quantum computers threaten RSA and elliptic curves.

tasks.title: Add two points and double a point on y^2 = x^3 + 2x + 2 over GF(17) and plot every point on the curve
Implement double-and-add scalar multiplication on a small curve and run an ECDH exchange between two parties, confirming both obtain the same point
Compare key and ciphertext sizes of RSA, ECDH and a lattice-based key encapsulation, and design a hybrid scheme for a payment app

schedule.title: Hashes and MACs
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: estimate birthday-bound collision effort for several hash sizes, and explain salted password hashing in your own words.

tasks.title: Find a collision in a hash truncated to 24 bits using the birthday attack and compare the number of tries with the theory
Show that a naive hash(key||message) MAC allows length extension, then fix it using HMAC and verify both against test vectors
Crack a list of unsalted password hashes with a dictionary, then repeat on salted bcrypt-style hashes and compare the time per guess

schedule.title: Signatures and PKI
schedule.exercise: Draw a certificate chain for a bank website and write a half-page assessment of what happens when a CA is compromised.

tasks.title: Sign and verify a short message with textbook RSA and a hash, then show the signature fails after changing a single character
Recover an ECDSA private key from two signatures that reused the same nonce, using the algebra of the signing equation
Configure a simulated client to trust a root CA, and trace validation of a three-link certificate chain that includes a revoked intermediate

schedule.title: TLS and secure protocols
schedule.exercise: Annotate a TLS 1.3 handshake diagram, labelling each key and the point where forward secrecy is gained.

tasks.title: Trace a TLS 1.3 handshake as packets between client and server in the network simulator and label the messages that carry key shares
Configure a server to refuse SSL3 and weak ciphers, then test a downgrade attempt by a simulated attacker and show it fails
Set up a WireGuard-style tunnel between two branch networks in the simulator and verify that traffic across the internet link is encrypted

schedule.title: DNS, email and protocol analysis
schedule.exercise: Review a short authentication protocol, name its attacker model and propose a fix for any replay or reflection weakness.

tasks.title: Inspect DNS and email records for a domain, identify the SPF and DKIM entries, and decide whether a sample message would pass DMARC
Replay a captured authentication message against a naive login protocol, then add a nonce challenge so the replay fails
Find Lowe's attack on the Needham-Schroeder protocol by tracing the message flow, then apply the fix and verify the attack no longer works

schedule.title: Key management
schedule.exercise: Write a key management policy for a small payments firm covering generation, storage, rotation and recovery.

tasks.title: Generate 128 bits from a weak entropy source and from a good one, then measure the entropy of each with a frequency test
Derive separate encryption and MAC keys from one master secret with HKDF and show that different context labels give unrelated keys
Split a secret into five Shamir shares with a threshold of three, reconstruct it from three shares, and show two shares reveal nothing

schedule.title: Applied cryptography and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone design document: a secure messaging or file-sharing tool with authenticated key exchange, authenticated encryption and a threat model.

tasks.title: Use a library-style API to encrypt and decrypt a message with authenticated encryption, then list three primitives you must never write yourself
Review a code listing of a toy messaging app, find five cryptographic mistakes such as ECB mode and hard-coded keys, and propose fixes
Design and simulate a secure file transfer between two hosts with authenticated key exchange and authenticated encryption, then test it against an active attacker
